chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Imran ibn Asim said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Four people are not answered [in prayer/claims]; one of them is a man who has wealth and then claims it back without proof.' He says, Allah, Exalted and Mighty, says: 'Did I not command you with testimony?'

key_terms.أَدَانَهُ: He claimed a debt or right against someone
key_terms.الشَّهَادَة: Testimony or witnessing, a key element in Islamic legal procedure
key_terms.بَيِّنَة: Proof or evidence, specifically referring to witnesses in legal contexts

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of lending money without witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the procedural validity of financial contracts to spiritual acceptance, specifically highlighting the neglect of witness testimony (*bayyinah*) as a cause for unanswered supplication. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that adherence to evidentiary standards in commerce is not merely a legal formality but a condition for divine favor, reinforcing the principle that justice in transactions is integral to piety.
